title: Introduce IO pressure matrix and inflight token trajectory dashboard
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Customers and SREs see intermittent tail latency correlated with GPU IO stalls and token inflight backpressure. Existing dashboards surfaced kernel and queue metrics but lacked a concise cross-stage view tying IO pressure to token-level inflight and tail-costs. This PR adds an IO Pressure Matrix (multi-dimensional heatmap) and an Inflight Token Trajectory dashboard to help correlate device IO metrics with token-level latency/cost, plus small tracing/log enrichment to improve root-cause signal. Summary of changes: 1) New Grafana panels: observability/dashboards/io-pressure-matrix.jsonnet and observability/dashboards/inflight-token-trajectory.jsonnet that show per-stage IO utilization, kernel queue depth, token-inflight histogram over time, and a token-lifecycle Sankey annotated with cost-per-stage. 2) New Prometheus metrics: serving_io_queue_depth{device,queue_type,priority}, token_inflight_count{model,route,priority}, token_latency_phase_seconds{phase} and derived recording rules for per-route percentiles. 3) Tracing: span_enricher now annotates spans with io_pressure and kernel_queue labels (serving/tracing/span_enricher.go) and a compact span attribute token_shard_id to reduce cardinality. 4) Logging: add structured log fields token_phase and shard_hint for sampled debug logs used by the interactive explorer. 5) Alert tuning: introduce two new alerts - High IO Pressure Matrix hotspot (alerts/io_pressure_hotspot.yaml) that uses sustained queue_depth/queue_wait_time and Token Trajectory drift alert (alerts/token_trajectory_drift.yaml) that triggers when p99 phase latency shifts > 2x for 10m with corroborating token_inflight increase. 6) Runtime: small change in the batching controller to emit token_inflight_count at batch commit time to avoid double-counting. Testing & validation: unit tests for metric exposition and recording rules added, e2e on dev cluster with synthetic replay (replay/fixtures/io_spike_run.yaml) and manual validation against production-like perf run; dashboards validated with real replay traces to ensure annotation linkage. Rollout plan: staged rollout - enable metric exposition behind feature flag observability.io_pressure_v2; enable dashboards for SRE beta workspace; alert defaults initially set to warn for 1 week while we monitor noise and tune thresholds. Links: design doc https://linear.app/redwood/issue/ENG-4207/io-pressure-matrix-design and runbook stub https://confluence.redwood.ai/obs/io-pressure-troubleshooting. Checklist: - [x] Add metrics and recording rules - [x] Dashboard panels and variable-driven queries - [x] Tracing/log enrichment and low-cardinality keys - [x] Unit and e2e tests - [x] Alert definitions and playbook entry - [x] Feature-flagged rollout and monitor window
commits: 3 commits: Add IO metrics and recording rules; Dashboard panels and templating; Trace/log enrichment and alert definitions
review_comments: Evan Morris: Looks good overall, please double-check cardinality on token_shard_id - can we bucket it to reduce dimension count?; Aisha: Yes - token_shard_id is now a 16-bin hash bucket in span_enricher (see commit 2); Jules Laurent: Alert thresholds look aggressive on p99 x2 — can we gate with a minimum sample count and add evaluation window?; Aisha: Added sample_count gating and extended window to 10m; Rina Kapoor: Dashboard variables are helpful but add a convenience toggle to switch between device and region grouping; Aisha: Added 'group_by' variable to both panels and updated docs with screenshots
ci_summary: CI: unit tests (pass), lint (pass), integration (pass on replay env), e2e-replay (manual validation) - no flaky tests observed; one ephemeral failure in a previous run re: metrics scrape timeout was fixed by increasing test scrape timeout
release_notes: Observability: Added IO Pressure Matrix and Inflight Token Trajectory dashboards, new IO and token inflight metrics, trace/log enrichment, and two tuned alerts to help diagnose IO-induced tail latency. Feature-flagged rollout and initial warn-level thresholds.
notes_for_oncall: If io_pressure_hotspot fires: 1) Check device-level queue_depth and queue_wait_time panels on IO Pressure Matrix, 2) Inspect Inflight Token Trajectory for sudden p99 jump and token_inflight spike, 3) Use trace links annotated with kernel_queue and io_pressure to correlate, 4) If sustained, consider routing policy to fallback model_variant or scale dedicated capacity. Playbook: docs/obs/io_pressure_runbook.md
